attributes.residual:
THE RESIDUAL IS NOW ONE INSTRUCTION AND ITS MECHANISM IS FULLY NAMED. Baseline is count-EXACT (T57/O57) and differs by exactly one opcode: the target spells a copy `addi`, we spell it `mr`. Aligned views, both read from the objects.

BASELINE, at the single use site: target `a4: addi r3,r31,0` / `a8: crclr 4*cr1+eq` / `ac: bl bulletproof_printf`, against ours `9c: lis r3,@lbl_801131C0(ADDR16_HA)` / `a0: crclr 4*cr1+eq` / `a4: addi r0,r3,@lbl_801131C0(ADDR16_LO)` / `a8: mr r3,r0` / `ac: bl bulletproof_printf`. Both sides spend THREE instructions on this address -- the target spends lis+addi in the PROLOGUE and one `addi r3,r31,0` at the use; we spend all three at the use. The target's prologue is `4: lis r4,@optionsAudioAndPrefs30(HA)` / `8: stw r0,4(r1)` / `c: lis r3,@lbl_801131C0(HA)` / `10: li r5,0` / `14: stwu r1,-32(r1)` / `18: stmw r30,24(r1)` / `1c: addi r30,r4,@optionsAudioAndPrefs30(LO)` / `20: addi r31,r3,@lbl_801131C0(LO)`: BOTH high halves are formed into DISTINCT volatiles before the frame is set up, and BOTH low halves are deferred until after stmw, where they can be written straight into callee-saved registers.

WHAT THE PROBES ACHIEVED, AND THE ONE THING THAT DEFEATS THEM. Initialising `st` at its declaration DOES buy the target's structure at the use site -- in all three probes the use site collapses to the target's single copy and the opcode multiset's target-only side goes EMPTY -- but it costs one instruction in the prologue instead: ours becomes `4: lis r3,@lbl_801131C0(HA)` / `8: stw r0,4(r1)` / `c: addi r0,r3,@lbl_801131C0(LO)` / `10: lis r3,@optionsAudioAndPrefs30(HA)` / `14: stwu` / `18: li r4,0` / `1c: li r5,0` / `20: stmw r30,24(r1)` / `24: addi r31,r3,@optionsAudioAndPrefs30(LO)` / `28: mr r30,r0`. We complete the FIRST address's @lo into r0 at +0xc -- BEFORE stmw, which is precisely the thing the predecessor record warned must not happen -- and then pay `mr r30,r0` to get it into its callee-saved home after stmw. The cause is visible in the register choice: OURS REUSES r3 FOR BOTH HIGH HALVES (+0x4 and +0x10), so the first result has to be evacuated before the second lis overwrites it, while the TARGET USES TWO DISTINCT VOLATILES (r4 and r3) and therefore has nothing to evacuate. That single evacuation is the whole +1, and it converts a count-exact function into a count-asymmetric one.

WHY THE ORDERING AXIS IS DEAD. Probes 1, 2 and 3 permuted declaration order, assignment order and local-block order and produced byte-identical objects every time, with `lis r3,@lbl_801131C0` at +0x4 in all three -- i.e. MWCC's choice of WHICH of the two addresses to compute first, and of which volatile to reuse, is invariant under every source ordering available here. It is not reverse-declaration order (probe 2 would have flipped it), not use order (opts is used first in the body and is nonetheless computed second in all three), and not local-block order (probe 3). The discriminant lies somewhere this function's source cannot reach by reordering.

The permutation class is excluded separately by the DIFFERING opcode multiset. This reproduces the predecessor's finding independently; that record also measured the raw count as 37 of 57 words differing with 29 unabsorbed.

hypothesis.statement: The evacuation is a volatile-register-reuse artefact, not an ordering one: ours puts both ADDR16_HA halves in r3 and must spill the first, while the target puts them in r4 and r3. What differs between the two address operands is their EXPRESSION CLASS, and that has not been varied -- `opts = &gameOpts` is an address-of applied to a named struct object, while `st = lbl_801131C0` is an array-to-pointer decay of an extern array. The untried form is to make the two operands the same class so MWCC schedules them symmetrically: spell the pool operand as an address-of its first element, `char* st = &lbl_801131C0[0];`, and if that is byte-identical (it may well be, being the same operand after decay), instead give the pool pointer a second, EARLIER use so its live range genuinely starts before the other's -- for example hoisting the `lbl_803449EC = 0;` store or the `sysClearFlags` argument through it -- since the sibling functions in this TU that get the target's prologue shape (add_vmu_file, writeGauntletSave) all have a `char* rpool = lbl_801131C0;` with MULTIPLE offset uses, and this is the only one with a single use at offset 0.
